title: Beyond the 956: Skip Hinnant, ‘The Electric Company’ star and voice of Fritz the Cat, dies at 86
excerpt: Skip Hinnant, the actor best known as an original cast member of PBS’ The Electric Company and the voice of Fritz the Cat, died peacefully November 8, 2026, in Denver at 86, according to his family obituary.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Skip Hinnant, the actor best known as an original cast member of the beloved PBS children’s series The Electric Company and the voice of Fritz the Cat, has died at 86.

Hinnant died peacefully on November 8, 2026, in Denver, Colorado, surrounded by his family, according to his family obituary, published through The New York Times. No cause of death was disclosed.

Born Joseph Howard Hinnant on September 12, 1940, in Chincoteague Island, Virginia, Hinnant built a career that spanned television, film, musical theater and voice work. He originated the role of Schroeder in the stage musical You’re a Good Man, Charlie Brown in 1967 before joining the original cast of The Electric Company, the Emmy-winning PBS series that ran from 1971 to 1977, where he played Fargo North, Decoder and a host of other characters.

In a sharp contrast with his children’s television work, Hinnant voiced the title character in Ralph Bakshi’s adult animated film Fritz the Cat (1972) and its sequel, The Nine Lives of Fritz the Cat (1974). He also voiced Sunny the Easter Bunny in the Rankin/Bass special The Easter Bunny Is Comin’ to Town (1977).

Hinnant is survived by his partner Ruth Nerken, his former wife Miriam Hinnant, four children and nine grandchildren.

Sources: Parade; The New York Times family obituary via Legacy.com.
